hook.line: This hashtag strategy got me millions of views.
hook.visual: Creator in a cap against a lit acoustic-panel wall; 'HASHTAG STRATEGY' title punches in with a hash sketch, then a view counter ticks 482K, 792K, 1M Views.

beats.what: Claim with a big two-colour title and an animated view counter climbing to 1M.
Objection named: 'as people say, hashtags don't matter' in red under white.
'How to use' title as he says you don't know how to use SEO.
Full-screen graphic: '9 HASHTAGS' glowing, then a 3 / 3 / 3 grid.
Grid fills column by column: topic of the video, in green.
Back to the face with his filled-in example table overlaid at the bottom.
'USE THIS FRAMEWORK' title over the table.
Blurred end card with his profile and a 'Following' button.

why_it_works: Result first with an animated counter (482K to 1M Views) proves the claim before any explanation.
Names the common objection ('hashtags don't matter') and flips it, creating tension in the first 6 s.
The whole method is one simple number pattern (9 = 3 + 3 + 3) built up column by column on screen, so it is easy to remember and screenshot.
A concrete filled-in example table over his face turns the framework into something copyable.
weaknesses: Graphics-only middle section drops the face for about 12 s.
Hashtag advice is thin and contestable; the hook overpromises.
The follow end card is a stock-looking popup.
for_robert: Build the core tip as a grid that fills one column per spoken item; Fred could drop each column's label in, then step aside when the face comes back.
